governing_question: How does Arkansas systematically increase the capability of its people and communities—and convert that capability into opportunity, ownership, productive capacity, belonging, and greater inheritance for the next generation?
central_proposition: A prosperous state needs capable people—not merely an available labor supply—and capital investment without community capacity can produce economic activity without producing a prosperous community.
organizing_sentence: Human & Community Capital joins child → education → capability → work → ownership → community → next generation into one continuous Arkansas system, informed by economic need without determining a person's life.

broader_human_capital_definition.rejects: Human capital = producing workers for employers

capability_continuum.title: Arkansas Capability Continuum
capability_continuum.rule: There is no single prescribed path. Education is not something people finish at 18 or 22—especially in an AI economy.
capability_continuum.movement_rule: People may move between pathways throughout life.

prior_ladder_join.rule: Not one forced path — multiple upward pathways, same objective
prior_ladder_join.objective: Increase the individual's capability to create value, exercise agency, acquire ownership and contribute to Arkansas

demand_map_architecture.title: Demand ↔ Capability Loop
demand_map_architecture.freedom_rule: Economic demand informs educational opportunity; it does not determine a person's life.
demand_map_architecture.hyp133_status: RELATIONSHIP_BOUND — empirical Demand Map build remains gated; do not invent county shortages
demand_map_architecture.adws_bridge_honesty: IPEDS↔ADWS family ratios are descriptive bridges, not shortage claims. County geographic gap = NEE.

education_financing_architecture.title: Intergenerational Arkansas Capital — education financing

layers.pre_k3_to_secondary: Publicly guaranteed for bona fide resident children — universal human-capital foundation.
layers.post_secondary_resident: Resident investment architecture based on bona fide domicile / public investment rate.
layers.nonresident_international: Premium capable of importing external revenue (Human-Capital External Income) — ILLUSTRATIVE until COUNTABLE clears.
layers.strategic_recruitment: Arkansas may deliberately invest in people it wants to become long-term Arkansans.

stage_4_tests: Legality of residency strength (Vlandis posture already noted)
Residency design / duration with proof of bona fide residence
education_financing_architecture.count_rule: No COUNTABLE tuition or external-income dollars in Pass 3.3.

research_to_prosperity.principle: Public participation in economic upside should bear a defensible relationship to public contribution and risk.

stages.label: Retain

stages.label: Return

counterarguments.strong_form: The state assigns lives to occupations via the Demand Map.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Freedom rule is explicit: demand informs opportunity; it does not determine a person's life. Multiple pathways remain open; ratios are not shortage mandates.
counterarguments.unresolved: STAGE_4 governance design of Demand Map updates

counterarguments.strong_form: Preferential resident rates freeze labor mobility and punish newcomers.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Frame is bona fide residency with proof pathway (Vlandis posture)—not permanent outsider labels. Belong stage converts arrival into membership.

counterarguments.claim: Public IP claims suppress research or commercialization.
counterarguments.strong_form: Labs flee if public upside is claimed.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Principle is proportionate public participation to public contribution/risk—not ownership of every invention. Exact IP structure deferred.

counterarguments.strong_form: Absentee scale always wins; localism shrinks productivity.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Worker→owner pathways coexist with employment and competitive enterprise. Efficiency without belonging can still fail Retain/Belong.
counterarguments.unresolved: STAGE_4 productivity comparisons by ownership form

counterarguments.claim: Government cannot accurately identify skills needs.
counterarguments.strong_form: Demand Maps lag and misallocate capacity.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Loop includes continuous update from market signals; descriptive bridges refuse shortage overclaim; county gaps labeled NEE.

counterarguments.strong_form: Benefits-for-service is forced labor by another name.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Principle is reciprocal investment, not conscription. Benefit design deferred; institutional rules differ by service type.

counterarguments.strong_form: More degrees without capability raise signaling costs.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Continuum emphasizes capability, multiple pathways, and demand-informed capacity—not credential volume alone.

counterarguments.claim: Rural communities cannot retain highly skilled workers.
counterarguments.strong_form: High skill always migrates to metros.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Place Capability Framework + Retain/Belong + Demand Map allow rural-specific opportunity design without pretending uniformity.

counterarguments.claim: AI changes the Demand Map faster than institutions can respond.
counterarguments.strong_form: Any skills system is obsolete on arrival.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Continuous reskilling + ownership + adaptability are the response; AI Social Compact stays on separate validation track.

open_validation_questions.question: How strong may bona fide residency requirements for subsidized higher education lawfully be in Arkansas?
What nonresident premium is lawful and economically viable without suppressing strategic attraction?
Can a county-resolved Demand Map be built without false shortage claims?
What public IP / royalty / equity share is proportionate to public contribution without suppressing commercialization?
Do CTE and multiple pathways improve household surplus and ownership vs credential-only tracks?
How should service-reciprocal benefits be designed without coercion?
